info.name: Sar7ny API (صارحني)
info.description:
Backend for the **Sar7ny** anonymous messaging app.

**Base URL** `{{baseUrl}}` — all endpoints live under `/api/v1`.

---

### Getting started

1. `npm run dev` (see README §5).
2. Run **01 Auth → Register**; `accessToken`, `refreshToken`, `userId` and `username` are stored automatically as collection variables by the response scripts.
3. Requests marked with bearer auth now work. Set `recipientUsername` to another account to receive messages and `messageId` / `reportId` / `targetUserId` from the responses you get.

---

### Conventions

- **Success**: `{"success": true, "message": "...", "data": {...}}`
- **Error**: `{"success": false, "message": "...", "code": "ERROR_CODE", "requestId": "..."}` (`details` appears for validation errors)
- Rate limits default to 300 global / 20 auth / 10 messages / 10 reports / 5 password per 15 minutes, per IP. Set `RATE_LIMIT_ENABLED=false` in `.env` while testing if you keep hitting `429 RATE_LIMITED`.
- Unknown fields are rejected, and `$`-operators / dotted keys are stripped from input (NoSQL-injection hardening).

---

**Google OAuth (folder 02)** needs `GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID`, `GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET` and `GOOGLE_REDIRECT_URI` to be set in `.env`; see README §10. It has not been exercised against Google's servers with real credentials.

item.name: 01 Auth
item.description:
JWT auth: 15-minute HS256 access token + opaque refresh token (stored server-side as a SHA-256 hash, rotated on every use).

Register/login/refresh are rate limited to `RATE_LIMIT_AUTH_MAX` (default 20) per 15 minutes, so the same IP may be throttled while you test.

request.description:
Creates an account. Change `username` / `email` to unique values before sending (a repeat answers `409`). `role` is always forced to `user` server-side — it can never be supplied here.

Password policy: 8-72 chars with at least one letter and one number.

On success the response variables `accessToken`, `refreshToken`, `userId` and `username` are stored automatically.

`identifier` accepts either the username or the email.

Unknown user and wrong password return byte-identical generic 401 responses (no account enumeration).

**Account Lockout**: 5 consecutive incorrect passwords temporarily ban the account for 5 minutes (`ACCOUNT_TEMPORARILY_BANNED`, HTTP 403).

**2-Step Verification (2FA)**:
- If 2FA is enabled: Returns `{ requiresTwoFactor: true, userId, loginTicket, email }` and sends a 6-digit OTP code to the email.
- If 2FA is disabled: Returns tokens immediately without extra steps.
Completes login when 2-Step Verification is enabled on the account. Requires the 6-digit OTP code sent to user email and either `loginTicket` or `userId`.
Sends a 6-digit OTP code to the authenticated user's email to initiate enabling 2-step verification.
Verifies the 6-digit OTP code and enables 2-step verification (`twoFactorEnabled: true`) for the authenticated user.
Disables 2-step verification (`twoFactorEnabled: false`) for the authenticated user.
Rotates the refresh token. The old one becomes invalid immediately; presenting it again is treated as token reuse and revokes the entire session chain.
Revokes the active refresh token and blacklists it in Redis.
Returns the authenticated user. 401 for a missing, expired, forged or disabled-account token.
Revokes all refresh tokens, increments user tokenVersion, and invalidates active sessions in Redis so every device is logged out.

item.name: 02 Google OAuth
item.description:
Sign in with Google (OAuth 2.0 / OpenID Connect).

**These endpoints are disabled until `GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID`, `GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET` and `GOOGLE_REDIRECT_URI` are all set** — otherwise they answer `400 OAUTH_NOT_CONFIGURED`.

The flow is browser-driven: `GET /` sets a signed HttpOnly flow cookie (`state` + PKCE `code_verifier` + `nonce`) and 302s to accounts.google.com, which redirects back to `/callback`. Two response modes:

- **JSON (default)** — the callback replies with the token pair directly.
- **Redirect** — set `OAUTH_REDIRECT_URL` and the callback 302s to your SPA with a one-time `handoff` code, redeemed by `POST /exchange`. Tokens are never placed in a URL.

See README section 10 for the Google Cloud Console setup and the exact redirect URI to register.

query.description: 1 if opening in a popup window, 0 for regular redirect

request.description:
**Open this in a browser, not in Postman.**

Returns `302` to accounts.google.com with `state`, `code_challenge` (S256) and `nonce` in the query, plus the `sarhny_oauth_flow` cookie (`HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax; Path=/api/v1/auth/google`).

A `redirect_uri` supplied in the query is ignored — it always comes from the environment.

**Only Google calls this** — the browser arrives here as part of the redirect chain.

Verifies the signed flow cookie against `state` (CSRF), checks the `iss` hint, exchanges the code server-side with the stored PKCE verifier, and verifies the ID token (signature, issuer, audience, expiry, nonce) using `google-auth-library`.

Failure codes: `OAUTH_STATE_MISMATCH` (400), `OAUTH_STATE_EXPIRED` (400), `OAUTH_ACCESS_DENIED` (400), `OAUTH_CODE_EXCHANGE_FAILED` (401), `OAUTH_ID_TOKEN_INVALID` (401), `OAUTH_EMAIL_NOT_VERIFIED` (401), `OAUTH_ACCOUNT_CONFLICT` (409), `OAUTH_ALREADY_LINKED` (409).

The flow cookie is cleared on every attempt, so a replayed callback fails.

Only used when `OAUTH_REDIRECT_URL` is set. The code is single-use, stored as a SHA-256 hash and expires after `OAUTH_HANDOFF_TTL_MS` (60s by default).

A link-purpose handoff returns `{linked: true}` **without** minting a new token pair — the caller is already authenticated. Unknown/reused codes return `401 OAUTH_HANDOFF_INVALID`.

Returns `{authorizationUrl}` for the browser to open; the flow cookie is set on this reply.

Linking is **explicit only** — a Google identity whose verified email matches an existing password account is never linked automatically (`409 OAUTH_ACCOUNT_CONFLICT`).

The body is `.strict()`: sending `role`, `isVerified` or any unknown field returns `400 VALIDATION_ERROR`.
Returns `{links, hasPassword}`. `hasPassword` is what guards unlinking.
Removed with `400 OAUTH_LAST_LOGIN_METHOD` when the account has no local password (lockout prevention), and `400 OAUTH_NOT_LINKED` when there is nothing to unlink.

item.name: 03 Users
item.description: Self-service routes plus the public profile.

request.description: Only `name`, `bio` and `avatar` are accepted (`avatar` must be an http(s) URL or empty). `role`, `isActive`, `isVerified` and `username` are rejected with `400 VALIDATION_ERROR`. Sending an empty body is also rejected.

Upload a profile picture (image file). Accepted: PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP — max 2 MB. The file is validated by magic bytes, so renamed scripts/HTML are refused. The stored reference replaces any previous avatar.

`currentPassword` is required for any account that already has a password. Omit it for a Google-only account that never had one — such callers are confirmed by their session alone; an empty string is rejected with 400 rather than treated as omitted. On success every other refresh token for the account is revoked (the session that made the change is kept).

Soft delete: `deletedAt` is set, sessions are revoked, and the account is wiped after `DELETED_ACCOUNT_RETENTION_DAYS` (30 by default). Response is generic. `password` is required for any account that already has one; omit it for a Google-only account.
No authentication. Returns the public view only (username, name, bio, avatar, createdAt) — never the email, role or account status. 404 for missing or disabled accounts.

item.name: 04 Messages
item.description:
Anonymous sending (the Message schema has **no sender field** — identity, IP and user agent are never persisted) plus the recipient's inbox.

Sending is rate limited to `RATE_LIMIT_MESSAGE_MAX` (default 10) per recipient per day.

request.description:
**Public and anonymous.** No access token required; supplying one does not record it.

The recipient username comes from the path (`{{recipientUsername}}`). Content is 1-2000 chars.

The response is only `{sent: true}` — **no message id is returned**, on purpose: an anonymous send must not hand the sender a handle into someone's inbox. Run *List my inbox* as the recipient and copy `data.messages[0]._id` into `{{messageId}}` for the requests below.

Returns the same generic 404 whether the recipient does not exist or has closed their inbox, so usernames cannot be probed.

**Cursor pagination** (not page/number). Drop `cursor` for the first page, then pass `data.nextCursor` from the previous response. `limit` is 1-50. `isRead` / `isArchived` are optional booleans.

Messages are at `data.messages[]`; copy `data.messages[0]._id` into `{{messageId}}` (an anonymous send never returns the id itself).
Scoped to the caller's own messages; anything else returns `404` (not 403) so ids cannot be probed.
No body. Idempotent.
`archived` defaults to `true`; send `false` to restore from the archive.
Logical delete — the document is marked deleted and removed from every listing.

item.name: 05 Reports
item.description:
Moderation. Anyone (anonymous or authenticated) can report; only admins can review.

Rate limited to `RATE_LIMIT_REPORT_MAX` (default 10) per salted fingerprint per day.

request.description:
**Works anonymously.** Auth is optional — a valid access token is attached as the reporter when present, otherwise the report is stored with no reporter identity.

`reason` must be one of: `harassment`, `threats`, `hate_speech`, `spam`, `sexual_content`, `other`. `details` is optional, max 1000 chars.

The report comes back at `data.report` with its identifier as **`id`** (not `_id`) — copy that value into `{{reportId}}` for the admin review requests.

Duplicate reports from the same source for the same message are rejected.
**Requires the `admin` role.** Page/limit pagination (`limit` max 100). `status`: `pending`, `reviewed`, `resolved`, `rejected`. Non-admins get `403`.
**Requires the `admin` role.** The report identifier is exposed as `data.report.id`.
**Requires the `admin` role.** Every change writes an `AuditLog` entry. `status` must be one of: `pending`, `reviewed`, `resolved`, `rejected`.

item.name: 06 Password
item.description:
One-time reset flow. **The response is always a generic 200** whether or not the email exists, so this endpoint cannot be used to discover accounts.

Rate limited to `RATE_LIMIT_PASSWORD_MAX` (default 5) per 15 minutes.

request.description: **Disabled.** Answers `503 PASSWORD_RESET_DISABLED` for every caller — existing account or not, Google or local — because there is no delivery channel left to send a link (email was removed from the project). Identical status and body either way, so it cannot be used to discover accounts. See README §11.

The token is single-use, stored hashed and validated against `expiresAt` + `usedAt` (MongoDB's TTL sweep is not trusted on its own because it is not immediate).

On success every refresh token for the account is revoked, forcing a re-login everywhere.
